title: 2 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 15.

questions.question: In what year of Jeroboam king of Israel did Azariah son of Amaziah begin to reign over Judah?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:1 states Azariah began to reign in the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel.

questions.question: How old was Azariah when he began to reign as king of Judah?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:2 says Azariah was sixteen years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: What was the name of Azariah's mother?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:2 mentions that Azariah's mother's name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.

questions.question: Did Azariah do what was right in the sight of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:3 states he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD according to all that his father Amaziah had done.

questions.question: What practice did the people continue that Azariah did not remove?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:4 says the high places were not removed and people sacrificed and burnt incense there.

questions.question: What affliction did the LORD give Azariah?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:5 tells that the LORD smote Azariah so that he was a leper until the day of his death.

questions.question: Who was over the house and judged the people while Azariah was afflicted?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:5 states Jotham the king's son was over the house, judging the people of the land.

questions.question: True or False: Azariah reigned for two and fifty years in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:2 confirms Azariah reigned for two and fifty years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:8 states Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in the thirty and eighth year of Azariah.

questions.question: True or False: Zachariah did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:9 says Zachariah did evil in the sight of the LORD, following the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

questions.question: Who conspired against and killed Zachariah?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:10 records Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against Zachariah, smote and slew him.

questions.question: The LORD spoke to Jehu saying that how many generations of his sons would sit on the throne of Israel?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:12 states the LORD told Jehu his sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation.

questions.question: How long did Shallum, son of Jabesh, reign in Samaria?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:13 says Shallum reigned a full month in Samaria.

questions.question: True or False: Shallum began to reign in the thirty and ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:13 states Shallum began to reign in the thirty and ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah.

questions.question: Which of these events occurred first according to 2 Kings 15?
options: Azariah began to reign over Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Azariah began to reign over Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:1 shows Azariah began to reign first; Zachariah reigned in 15:8, Shallum killed Zachariah in 15:10, and Menahem killed Shallum after that (15:14).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the consequence of Menahem's violent attack on Tiphsah as described in 2 Kings 15?
options: He took Tiphsah as his capital city
He spared the women and children
He brutally killed all the inhabitants including pregnant women
He made peace with Tiphsah's leaders
questions.correctAnswer: He brutally killed all the inhabitants including pregnant women
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:16 states that Menahem smote Tiphsah and all therein, and ripped up all the women with child because they would not open to him. This shows the severity of his violence and lack of mercy.

questions.question: How does Menahem's action toward Pul king of Assyria illustrate a practical lesson about securing power or protection?
options: Menahem trusted solely in God without paying tribute
Menahem bribed Pul with money to secure his kingdom
Menahem formed a military alliance without payment
Menahem ignored the threat and prepared defenses
questions.correctAnswer: Menahem bribed Pul with money to secure his kingdom
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 15:19-20, Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver to confirm his kingdom and exacted money from Israel to pay this tribute. This suggests reliance on worldly means to maintain power, teaching caution about trusting in human resources alone.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 15:18 teach us about obedience and its consequences for a king's reign?
options: Menahem fully obeyed God and prospered
He did evil and departed from God's commands leading to ongoing sin
He was indifferent to God's commands but prospered
He followed the sins of Judah instead of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He did evil and departed from God's commands leading to ongoing sin
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states Menahem did evil in the sight of the LORD and departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, implying that disobedience leads to continued sin and God's displeasure, warning believers about the importance of obedience.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 15, what lesson about leadership and integrity can be learned from the assassinations of kings like Shallum and Pekahiah?
options: Kings who rule justly are never overthrown
Conspiracies and violent power grabs reflect instability from ungodly leadership
Assassinations were part of God's plan to reward the righteous
Peaceful transitions of power are guaranteed
questions.correctAnswer: Conspiracies and violent power grabs reflect instability from ungodly leadership
questions.explanation: Verses 14, 25 show Shallum and Pekahiah were killed by conspirators, indicating that ungodly, evil leadership often leads to violent upheaval, underscoring the value of integrity and faithfulness in leadership (2 Kings 15:14, 25).

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 15:24 reveal about Pekahiah's reign and its spiritual implications?
options: Pekahiah did right before the LORD
He did evil and continued Israel's sinful traditions
He brought Israel back to true worship
He was neutral in religious matters
questions.correctAnswer: He did evil and continued Israel's sinful traditions
questions.explanation: Verse 24 states Pekahiah did evil in the sight of the LORD and departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, teaching that continuation in sin leads to judgment and downfall.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 15:15, the conspiracies and acts of Shallum were well documented.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:15 explicitly states that the acts and conspiracy of Shallum are written in the chronicles of the kings of Israel, confirming documentation of these events.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 15:20 illustrate the burden placed on Israel's wealthy men during Menahem's reign?
options: They were required to pay fifty shekels of silver each
They were forced to serve in the army
They freely donated to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They were required to pay fifty shekels of silver each
questions.explanation: Verse 20 explains that Menahem exacted fifty shekels of silver from each mighty man of wealth to pay the king of Assyria, showing the heavy financial burdens imposed on the wealthy to secure political favor.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 15:21 imply about the historical records of Menahem's reign?
options: They are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
They are only recorded in the book of the kings of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: They are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
questions.explanation: The verse states all that Menahem did are recorded in the chronicles of Israel's kings, emphasizing the importance of historical record-keeping for accountability and teaching.

questions.question: What is the significance of Pekahiah's assassination occurring 'in the palace of the king's house' as indicated in 2 Kings 15:25?
options: It shows the conspiracy was external and unexpected
It indicates betrayal within the king's own circle
It was a public execution approved by the people
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates betrayal within the king's own circle
questions.explanation: Verse 25 notes Pekah, a captain under Pekahiah, conspired against and killed him in the palace, showing intimate betrayal and the dangers of disloyalty from close associates.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 15:22 and 23 together show the pattern of succession in Israel's monarchy during this period?
options: Succession was always peaceful and hereditary
Kings often reigned for many decades without issue
The throne passed from father to son but was unstable
Kings were elected by the people
questions.correctAnswer: The throne passed from father to son but was unstable
questions.explanation: Verse 22 says Menahem died and was succeeded by his son Pekahiah (verse 23), but given the frequent assassinations, the hereditary succession was often marked by instability and violence.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 15:26, the acts of Pekahiah were not recorded anywhere.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:26 states that the acts of Pekahiah are recorded in the chronicles of the kings of Israel, confirming the documentation of his reign.

questions.question: Based on 2 Kings 15:17-19, how does the chapter illustrate the relationship between Israel's kings and foreign powers?
options: Israel's kings always defeated foreign enemies without aid
They sometimes paid tribute to foreign kings to secure their reigns
Foreign kings were never involved in Israel's affairs
Israel formed alliances based solely on shared faith
questions.correctAnswer: They sometimes paid tribute to foreign kings to secure their reigns
questions.explanation: Verses 19-20 show Menahem paying Pul king of Assyria a large sum to secure his kingdom, highlighting the political realities and compromises kings made with foreign powers.

questions.question: What practical Christian lesson about leadership can be drawn from the repeated statement that kings did evil and departed not from the sins of Jeroboam in 2 Kings 15?
options: Leaders must rely on their own wisdom rather than God's guidance
Continuing in known sin leads to downfall and God's displeasure
It is acceptable for leaders to follow the majority's ways
Sin has no effect on the stability of a kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Continuing in known sin leads to downfall and God's displeasure
questions.explanation: Multiple verses (e.g., 15:18, 15:24, 15:28) stress that kings who persisted in sinning after Jeroboam caused Israel to sin, teaching that persistent disobedience has serious consequences and leaders must pursue righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 15:23, Pekahiah reigned over Israel for ten years.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:23 states Pekahiah reigned two years, not ten, indicating a short and unstable reign.

questions.question: How does the violent pattern of kingship seen in 2 Kings 15:14-25 challenge believers to consider the biblical virtues of humility and integrity in leadership?
options: It shows that power is best maintained by violence
It warns that pride and corruption lead to downfall and instability
It encourages leaders to seek revenge for wrongs
It suggests leadership is unimportant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: It warns that pride and corruption lead to downfall and instability
questions.explanation: The frequent assassinations and conspiracies reflect pride and evil leadership, teaching that humility, integrity, and God-fearing conduct are essential for stable, godly leadership (2 Kings 15:14, 15:25).

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who began to reign in the two and fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah over Israel in Samaria?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:27 states that in the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria.

questions.question: What was the nature of Pekah's reign according to 2 Kings 15?
options: He did evil in the sight of the LORD
He did right in the sight of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He did evil in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:28 clearly states Pekah did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

questions.question: Which king of Assyria invaded during Pekah's reign and took multiple cities captive?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:29 mentions Tiglathpileser king of Assyria came against Israel during Pekah's reign and captured many cities.

questions.question: Who conspired against Pekah and killed him to become king in his place?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:30 tells that Hoshea the son of Elah conspired against Pekah, smote and slew him, and reigned in his stead.

questions.question: At what age did Jotham son of Uzziah begin to reign over Judah?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:33 states Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which of the following did Jotham do during his reign according to 2 Kings 15?
options: He did right in the sight of the LORD and built the higher gate of the house of the LORD
He removed all high places and abolished idol worship
He was a leper and lived in a separate house
He reigned only two years before being killed
questions.correctAnswer: He did right in the sight of the LORD and built the higher gate of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:34-35 describes Jotham doing right in the sight of the LORD and building the higher gate of the house of the LORD, though high places were not removed.

questions.question: Which external kingdom began to send threats against Judah during Jotham's reign?
options: Syria under Rezin and Israel under Pekah
questions.correctAnswer: Syria under Rezin and Israel under Pekah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:37 reports that the LORD began to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah in Jotham's days.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 15 connect with the prophecy in 2 Kings 10:30 about Jehu's descendants?
options: It fulfills Jehu's prophecy that his sons would sit on Israel's throne for four generations
It contradicts Jehu's prophecy by having no descendants reign
It foretells the destruction of Jehu's line within one generation
It shows Jehu's descendants reigning only in Judah, not Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Jehu's prophecy that his sons would sit on Israel's throne for four generations
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:12 references the LORD's word to Jehu that his sons would sit on Israel's throne for four generations, which is fulfilled in this chapter through the reigns of Jehu's descendants.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'high places' (Hebrew: bamot) in this chapter's context?
options: They were unauthorized worship sites where people sacrificed, disobeying central worship laws
They were designated holy sites approved by the LORD
They were marketplaces for trade and commerce
They were fortresses built to defend cities
questions.correctAnswer: They were unauthorized worship sites where people sacrificed, disobeying central worship laws
questions.explanation: The 'high places' (bamot) mentioned in 2 Kings 15:4 and 15:35 refer to unauthorized local shrines where the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense, contrary to the LORD's commands for centralized worship.

questions.question: Which king exacted fifty shekels of silver from Israel's wealthy men to pay tribute to the king of Assyria?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:20 describes Menahem exacting fifty shekels of silver from each wealthy man in Israel to pay tribute to the king of Assyria, Pul.

questions.question: Which violent act is attributed to Menahem in this chapter?
options: He ripped open all pregnant women in Tiphsah
He destroyed the temple of the LORD
He killed Jotham king of Judah
He burned the city of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He ripped open all pregnant women in Tiphsah
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 15:16, Menahem attacked Tiphsah because they did not open the city to him, and he cruelly ripped open all the women that were with child.

questions.question: True or False: Jotham removed all the high places during his reign.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:35 states that although Jotham did right in the sight of the LORD, the high places were not removed, and people still sacrificed and burned incense there.

questions.question: True or False: Pekah reigned twenty years over Israel in Samaria according to this chapter.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:27 records that Pekah reigned twenty years over Israel in Samaria.

questions.question: Which Bible passage echoes the theme of kings doing 'evil in the sight of the LORD' as seen with multiple kings in 2 Kings 15?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:34 similarly describes several kings of Israel doing evil in the sight of the LORD, paralleling the repeated theme in 2 Kings 15.

questions.question: How does the reign of Pekah and the Assyrian invasions foreshadow later Israelite history?
options: It foreshadows the eventual Assyrian exile of Israel
It signals the building of Solomon's temple
It marks the start of the Davidic dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the eventual Assyrian exile of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:29 shows Tiglathpileser's invasion and captives being taken, foreshadowing the later full Assyrian exile of Israel in 2 Kings 17.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD when He smote King Azariah with leprosy, causing him to dwell separately until his death?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:5 shows God smiting Azariah with leprosy, a judgment reflecting God's holiness and intolerance of sin even in a king who 'did that which was right' but failed in removing high places.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 15, what recurring sin did several kings of Israel fail to depart from, demonstrating the persistent nature of human rebellion?
options: Sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
questions.correctAnswer: Sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
questions.explanation: Verses 9, 18, 24, and 28 repeatedly mention Israelite kings doing evil by not departing from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, illustrating humanity's repeated rebellion against God's covenant.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by the LORD's word to Jehu that his descendants would sit on Israel's throne to the fourth generation?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:12 records a prophetic word from God to Jehu promising his sons' dynasty would last four generations, illustrating God's covenant faithfulness even amid Israel's unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Menahem’s violent actions against Tiphsah (2 Kings 15:16) reflect on the biblical teaching about the consequences of sin and human depravity?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:16 details Menahem’s brutal massacre and cruelty, exemplifying how sin corrupts human hearts and leads to worsening violence and injustice.

questions.question: What does the repeated failure to remove high places by kings like Azariah and Jotham (2 Kings 15:4, 35) signify about Israel's sanctification process?
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 35 show that although Azariah and Jotham did right in the LORD’s sight, they did not remove high places, indicating an incomplete sanctification with persistent compromise in worship practices.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is revealed by God allowing Assyria to invade and carry captives from Israel during Pekah’s reign (2 Kings 15:29)?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:29 records Tiglathpileser king of Assyria capturing Israelite cities, reflecting God's justice in punishing Israel for persistent sin and covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does the reign of Jotham, who did right but did not remove high places (2 Kings 15:34-35), contribute to the biblical understanding of sanctification as both positional and progressive?
options: Sanctification involves continual growth despite imperfection
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves continual growth despite imperfection
questions.explanation: Jotham's reign (2 Kings 15:34-35) shows he did right in God's sight but failed to fully remove sinful worship sites, illustrating sanctification as a progressive journey rather than instantaneous perfection.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the Bible's depiction of God allowing violent political coups (e.g., killing of kings in 2 Kings 15) shows divine endorsement of violence. What does 2 Kings 15 actually teach about God's sovereignty and human sinfulness?
options: God is sovereign over human evil but does not approve it
questions.correctAnswer: God is sovereign over human evil but does not approve it
questions.explanation: Verses like 2 Kings 15:10 and 15:25 show violent coups, but the text presents these as results of human sin and divine judgment, not divine approval, affirming God's sovereignty over history and human sinfulness (cf. Romans 8:28).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Kings 15:19 and 15:20 provide regarding the relationship between human political power and divine sovereignty?
options: Divine sovereignty permits human rulers to seek foreign alliances that test their faithfulness
Political power is irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Divine sovereignty permits human rulers to seek foreign alliances that test their faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:19-20 recount Menahem paying tribute to Assyria for political security, showing that while humans maneuver politically, God's sovereignty oversees and allows these events as tests of faithfulness and judgment.

questions.question: How do the reigns of Azariah and Pekah (2 Kings 15:1, 27) illustrate the biblical teaching about the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness over generations?
options: Unfaithfulness leads to judgment and exile over time
God resets history after each king
questions.correctAnswer: Unfaithfulness leads to judgment and exile over time
questions.explanation: Azariah and Pekah’s reigns show ongoing sin and rebellion (2 Kings 15:1, 27), culminating in invasions and exile (15:29), illustrating covenant consequences across generations as part of divine discipline.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'slept with his fathers' (e.g., 2 Kings 15:7, 22) typologically communicate about death and the hope of resurrection in the biblical narrative?
options: Death is final and without hope
Death is a temporary rest anticipating resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Death is a temporary rest anticipating resurrection
questions.explanation: The euphemism 'slept with his fathers' in verses like 2 Kings 15:7 reflects the biblical hope that death is not the end but a temporary sleep before resurrection (cf. 1 Thessalonians 4:13-14).

questions.question: What narrative arc does the sending of Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah in Jotham's days (2 Kings 15:37) contribute to in the grand redemptive story?
options: The rise of Israel's golden age
The prophetic fulfillment of judgment preceding exile
questions.correctAnswer: The prophetic fulfillment of judgment preceding exile
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:37 shows external threats intensifying during Jotham’s reign, contributing to the narrative of divine judgment leading to exile, a key theme in God's redemptive plan (cf. Isaiah 7).

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine justice and mercy do 2 Kings 15:5 and 2 Kings 15:38 convey regarding God's dealings with kings who do right yet retain sin?
options: God punishes without warning or mercy
God allows consequences but provides continuity through successors
questions.correctAnswer: God allows consequences but provides continuity through successors
questions.explanation: Azariah’s leprosy judgment (15:5) reflects justice, but Jotham's succession (15:38) shows God’s mercy in preserving the Davidic line, balancing judgment with covenantal continuity.

questions.question: Which doctrine is exemplified by the chronicling of the acts of various kings in 'the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel/Judah' as repeatedly mentioned in 2 Kings 15 (e.g., verses 6, 11, 21, 26, 31, 36)?
questions.explanation: The references to the chronicles (e.g., 2 Kings 15:6, 11) show God's providential control over historical records and kings' reigns, underscoring His sovereign governance over human history.

questions.question: What theological insight about human covenant failure and divine judgment can be drawn from the rapid succession of kings assassinated and replaced in Israel (2 Kings 15:8-30)?
options: God’s judgment manifests in political instability due to covenant unfaithfulness
Kingship is divinely guaranteed to be peaceful
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment manifests in political instability due to covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The swift assassinations and reign changes (2 Kings 15:8-30) reflect God’s judgment on Israel for persistent covenant disobedience, revealing how sin disrupts societal order.
